description: Guide a student to find and fix a timezone misalignment bug in a crypto-stock correlation analysis where BTC (UTC) and AAPL (Eastern Time) data are merged on calendar date without timezone conversion, causing a 1-day shift.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I'm trying to compare Bitcoin and AAPL prices to see if they're correlated. I merged them by date but the correlation seems weird — sometimes negative when I expect positive. Can you help me check my merge?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I'm computing BTC-AAPL correlation by merging on calendar date, but my results differ from what Bloomberg shows. The BTC data is in UTC and AAPL data is in Eastern Time. Could there be a timezone issue in my merge?
student_openings.advanced_quant: My cross-asset correlation analysis shows spurious results. I suspect a systematic misalignment between my UTC crypto timestamps and US Eastern equity close timestamps when joining on calendar date. Can you help me diagnose the temporal alignment?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student identifies that BTC UTC timestamps and AAPL Eastern Time timestamps need tz_convert before extracting date for merging, understands the 1-day offset, and fixes the code.
required_capabilities: Read the timezone_merge code and understand both data sources
Identify the timezone mismatch in the merge key extraction
Explain why 00:00 UTC maps to previous day in Eastern Time
Verify correlation changes after the fix
